newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-MUSTER BOOSTS CONFIDENCE WITH HARD-FOUGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER BOOSTS CONFIDENCE WITH HARD-FOUGHT WIN.

text.p: Thomas Muster showed glimpses of the tenacity which once made him king on the Paris clay to move past German Marc-Kevin Goellner in five sets in an exciting first round match at the French Open on Monday.
Austrian Muster, the 1995 champion, proved he remains a formidable competitor by shrugging off a fierce challenge from the unseeded Goellner to pull off a 4-6 7-6 6-2 6-7 6-4 win.
Both players received a standing ovation from the crowd at the end of a superb fight which spanned over three hours on a beautiful afternoon.

Muster, almost unbeatable on clay in recent years but not quite as mighty since he opted to improve his game on other surfaces, made a poor start, losing the first set 6-4 and going 5-4 down in the second.
"After losing the first set, I just concentrated on my own game and on what I had to do," explained Muster, seeded fifth this year.
His trademark, powerful ground strokes accompanied by noisy grunts allowed him to force a tie-break in the second set, which he won 7-4.

He then moved on top of Goellner to win a one-sided third set 6-2 before the hard-hitting German, feeling he had a rare opportunity of beating a top 10 player, recovered by firing aces almost at will in the next set, which he took 7-2 in a tie-break.

Goellner must have thought he had his man when he broke Muster in the deciding set to open up a 4-2 lead, but the Austrian once again lived up to his reputation as one of the toughest fighters around.
He levelled it at 4-4, then broke Goellner to lead 5-4 and serve for the match. On his second match point, Muster saw the tiring German hit a forehand pass too long.

"The key to the match was fitness and concentration," said Goellner. "When I managed that break in the last set, I rejoiced a little too soon and my concentration dropped. He then started to play extremely well and he won. I know he never gives up but I was not careful enough."

Muster, not exactly the friendliest character in the game, patted Goellner on the shoulder before shaking his hand and smiling at him after winning the match, as if he wanted to congratulate him for putting up such a brave fight.

"It's a very important win, just the kind I needed to boost my confidence," Muster explained. "I got into the match slowly but I played better every set and I'm pretty satisfied with the way it went."
Muster was relatively successful early in the season in the hardcourt events but, surprisingly enough, started to struggle when the clay season came.
"I've not been very good on clay so far, partly because I've been struggling to adapt to that surface after the hardcourt season," he said. "I've also had a few health problems but I'm fine now."

Asked if he thought he could win the tournament, Muster forced a smile. "That kind of problem is not on my mind at the moment," he said. "I'm looking forward to a day off tomorrow and hoping I'll have something good for breakfast."
